timeline.text:
End of an era. Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO. Today John Ternus takes over.

Here's the pattern nobody is talking about.

Apple doesn't pick CEOs. It picks weapons for the next war.

Late 1990s. Apple was dying. It brought back Steve Jobs. A product visionary who saved the company by building things people didn't know they needed.

Apple had the best products but needed global scale.

It picked Tim Cook. An operations guy who turned it into a $5 trillion supply chain machine. $350 billion to $5 trillion on his watch. First company to cross $1T, $2T, $3T.

Apple has the best devices on earth and the weakest AI narrative in big tech.

So it picked an engineer.

John Ternus. 25 years at Apple.

He led the shift to Apple Silicon. Killed Intel. Shipped the M1. Hardware lead on every iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Vision Pro of the last decade.

The same week he becomes CEO, OpenAI and Anthropic are buying tens of thousands of his Mac minis to train AI agents. Apple hardware became critical AI infrastructure without Apple building a single AI model.

The AI war won't be won by chatbots. It'll be won on the chips AI runs on.

Ternus built those chips.

Tim Cook's last words as CEO: "My title changes tomorrow, but the love I have for the Apple community never will."

The hardest shoes in tech were handed to the quietest engineer in the room.
